input: Investigate crowdfunding platforms for my documentary project

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a first scan of all options or a deep-dive comparison of shortlisted platforms changes how broad or detailed the research should be.
Whether the documentary is a solo passion project, a team production, or tied to an organisation affects which platforms allow multiple collaborators and how funds are managed.
The documentary's subject matter and genre (e.g. social issue, arts, journalism) determines which niche or general platforms are the best fit.
The funding target amount shapes which platforms are realistic — some are better for micro-campaigns, others for six-figure goals — and affects fee impact.
Whether the campaign needs to launch imminently or is in early planning affects how urgently platforms must be evaluated and whether there is time to build an audience first.
A preference for all-or-nothing funding vs. keep-what-you-raise models, or for equity vs. rewards-based crowdfunding, is a fundamental filter that immediately narrows the platform list.
Knowing the desired output — e.g. a ranked shortlist, a comparison spreadsheet, or a go/no-go recommendation — determines how the research should be packaged and what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Investigate crowdfunding platforms for documentary project
gold.taskDescription: Research and evaluate crowdfunding platforms suited to funding a documentary film project.

questions.title: What is the documentary's subject matter or genre?
questions.description: Identify the topic and genre of the documentary (e.g. social justice, nature, personal story, investigative journalism) to match it with platforms that specialise in or have a strong audience for that content type.

questions.title: What total funding amount are you trying to raise?
questions.description: Establish the funding goal (e.g. under $10K, $10K–$50K, $50K+) to filter platforms by their typical campaign size, fee structures, and realistic audience reach.

questions.title: Do you want all-or-nothing or keep-what-you-raise funding?
questions.description: Determine the preferred campaign model — all-or-nothing (funds returned if goal is not met) vs. flexible/keep-what-you-raise — as this is a primary filter that immediately eliminates many platforms.

questions.title: Is this a solo project or does a team or organisation need access?
questions.description: Clarify who the campaign owner is and whether multiple collaborators, a production company, or a fiscal sponsor need to be involved, which affects account structure and payout options.

questions.title: When do you plan to launch the campaign?
questions.description: Identify the intended launch timeline (e.g. within weeks, 3–6 months, no set date) to prioritise how quickly platforms must be evaluated and whether audience-building steps should be included in the plan.

questions.title: Should this cover all platforms or focus on film-specific ones?
questions.description: Decide whether the investigation should span general crowdfunding platforms (e.g. Kickstarter, Indiegogo) alongside film-specific ones (e.g. Seed&Spark, Slated) or concentrate only on industry-focused options.

questions.title: What should the final output of this research look like?
questions.description: Define what a successful deliverable looks like — e.g. a ranked shortlist, a side-by-side comparison table, a single platform recommendation with rationale — so the research is packaged in the most useful way.
